problem: Prior embodied dialog localization (LED on WAY, LingUNet) needs the entire dialog before predicting a single location, which is impractical for a deployed locator who refines their belief turn by turn; single-shot models also over-fit to the small WAY dataset.
motivation: Search-and-rescue style collaborative localization benefits from estimating or narrowing the location after each turn, enabling early stopping and helping generate the next question. Turn-wise predictions also expose uncertainty and reduce the compute of re-encoding the full dialog.
key_idea: Cast dialog localization as iterative multi-shot prediction: a Transformer fusion encoder (ViT map + frozen BERT dialog) updates a hidden state each turn and outputs a location heatmap after every turn.
insight: Iterative fusion generalizes better to unseen maps than single-shot: DiaLoc-e (explicit fusion with a fixed map embedding times a hidden state) beats DiaLoc-i (purely implicit recurrence) on valUnseen, while implicit fusion over-fits on valSeen. The auxiliary MSE loss, which keeps early predictions diverse, improves results in most decay settings (Table 4), and fine-tuning ViT matters a lot. A non-zero decay lowers accuracy because of early convergence.
method: Unimodal encoders: ImageNet-21k ViT-base (fine-tuned) encodes the 224x224 top-down map into 196 tokens; frozen BERT-base encodes each dialog turn (max 100 tokens).
Multimodal fusion encoder: N Transformer blocks with self-attention, cross-attention (text query, map key/value) and FF layers, producing hidden state S with the same shape as the visual embedding.
DiaLoc-e (explicit): S_t = Phi(V ⊙ S_{t-1}, L_t), with S initialised to 1 as a prior over the map.
DiaLoc-i (implicit): S_t = Phi(S_{t-1}, L_t), recurrently conditioned on all turns.
Prediction head: conv/deconv layers convert S_t to a heatmap H; the location is Argmax(Softmax(H)).

Multi-shot loss: KL divergence to a Gaussian-smoothed (3 m) target at every turn, decay-weighted by alpha^(T-t), plus an auxiliary MSE loss (weight beta) on Sigmoid(H)⊙mask to keep early predictions diverse.
Dialog augmentation: gpt-3.5-turbo-16k paraphrases the training dialogs (temperature 0.6, top-p 0.5), sampled randomly against the ground-truth dialog.

setting.backbone: ViT-base (ImageNet-21k, fine-tuned) + BERT-base-uncased (frozen) + Transformer fusion encoder, trained on WAY
setting.training_data: WAY train split (9,955 dialogs); optional GPT-3.5 paraphrased dialogs as augmentation
setting.observation: top-down floor map (224x224) + dialog text per turn
setting.action_space: none (localization heatmap over the map, argmax pixel)
setting.privileged: known target floor map and per-turn ground-truth locations used for training/evaluation

numbers.method: DiaLoc-e (multi-shot, final prediction, d=3, alpha=0, beta=1)
numbers.extra: target-floor setting; multi-shot final turn; Acc0/Acc5 (not LE-threshold on all floors)
numbers.evidence: Table 2 (Evaluations on WAY dataset under single-shot and multi-shot): DiaLoc-e 18.36 60.00 8.44 47.15

numbers_note: Results are only on the WAY val splits (not the test split; the test set lacks target floor and per-turn locations). The abstract's +7.08 (single-shot) and +10.85 (multi-shot) Acc5 valUnseen gains are consistent with Table 2. LE values appear only in the ablation tables.
results: On WAY valUnseen, single-shot DiaLoc (BLIP(DiaLoc)) reaches Acc5 40.41 vs LingUNet 33.33 (+7.08). Multi-shot DiaLoc-e reaches Acc5 47.15 vs the strongest multi-shot baseline LingUNet-e at 36.30 (+10.85), and it also beats the single-shot LingUNet. Multi-shot needs less text-attention compute than re-encoding the full dialog, but it uses more memory and runtime.
limitations: Evaluated only on the WAY val splits with the known target floor; no test-set results because the test split lacks floor and per-turn location annotations.
Higher inference cost than LingUNet-ms (1.374 s vs 0.768 s, 3,875 vs 1,273 MiB); performance degrades on long dialogs (T=6) due to unbalanced training data.
Interim predictions are evaluated only by argmax, which is unfair when several peaks exist; the paper leaves early-stopping and question generation to future work.
